newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian Savings Bank active as shares rise.
newsitem.headline: Estonian Savings Bank active as shares rise.

text.p: The Estonian stock market was active again on Monday and Savings Bank was the most traded after it made a forecast for higher 1997 earnings, dealers said.
The Tallinn stock exchange index rose by one percent to 145.59 and the main list total volume reached 32.3 million kroons.
Savings Bank earlier said its next year group profit would be 140 million kroons and it was the most traded with turnover of 15.8 million kroons and closed at 64.75 kroons versus 64.30.
"Savings Bank next year forecast was nothing new and today it had no big impact on its share, but we might see changes tomorrow," Tonu Pekk, chief of equities for Hansapank, told Reuters.
Savings Bank had made a profit of 55.47 million kroons after 11 months of activity this year.
Forekspank was also active on trading of 7.7 million kroons and it ended higher at 104.10 kroons versus 102.
Market leader Hanspank turned over some 5.6 million kroons and closed up at 145.50 kroons versus 143.50.
The over-the-counter market saw trade of 19.9 million kroons and the Norma plastics maker was the most traded stock on volume of 9.6 million kroons but it closed lower at 35.40 kroons against 35.05.
The Tallinna Kaubamaja department store turned over three million kroons and rose to close at 74.50 kroons against 72.25.
